messages:
support-alice: FYI — AcmeCorp hitting lots of 503s on hosted inference since ~09:40 UTC. CS ticket #4572. Their logs show worker exits and container restarts. Paging @ryan :fire:
oncall-ryan: on it. Can you post the failing run id / pod name if you have it?
support-alice: run_id=acme-req-2079, pod=hosted-infer-rt-5f7b9, region=us-west-2. I grabbed last few lines of kube logs: `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` then `CUDA out of memory` and container restart loop.
eng-runtime-jordan: :eyes: thanks. Likely upstream worker crash during large-toolcall. Can someone grab `kubectl describe pod` + `kubectl logs --previous` and NVML output? Also check node dmesg for OOM/kern messages.
sre-maria: grabbing now. small snippets: ```kubectl logs hosted-infer-rt-5f7b9 --previous -n hosted-infer
[2026-03-18T09:39:50Z] runtime: runtime.cc:482] ATTENTION: received SIGABRT
[2026-03-18T09:39:50Z] error: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-18T09:39:50Z] Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
eng-runtime-jordan: OK pattern: OOM then segfault during error path. Possibly KV prefetch + large batch + 16k streaming context. For immediate mitigation: (1) route Acme traffic to fallback pool (cpu/smaller model) (2) disable prefetch on the worker pool (3) reduce max_concurrency for that pool. I'll open routing change.
deploy-bot: Routing change submitted: canary -> fallback-pool for customer=AcmeCorp (rollout id r-6621).
support-alice: Communicated to customer: temporary degraded perf but requests accepted; CS will update.
oncall-ryan: I see the node has repeated cuda errors in dmesg: "NVRM: Xid 79: GPU page fault" and driver reset. Also kube events show container OOMKilled then CrashLoopBackOff.
eng-runtime-jordan: Please capture core and nvcrash logs from the node. Command I want run on node: ```sudo journalctl -u docker -n 200; sudo /usr/bin/nvml-smi -q; sudo gcore -p $(pgrep -f infer-runner) <pid> || echo no-pid``` — but do only if safe. Also capture model weights in-use and quantization variant.
sre-maria: grabbing core and nodal logs now. Provisional root cause hypothesis: a memory blowout in attention kernel when prefetch tries to map a very large context + dynamic batching spike. Not confident yet.
eng-runtime-jordan: For hotfix we should: reduce batch cap to 4, disable KV prefetch for hot shards, and restart the pool gracefully. I'll prepare a config patch.
cs-lead-tom: Noted — I'll send a short customer update (ETA 30m) and offer retry window.
oncall-ryan: Implemented temporary pool limits: `max_concurrency=4, max_batch_tokens=8192, prefetch=false` on pool hosted-infer-usw2-1. Restarted 3/5 replicas, monitoring. :+1:
support-alice: After routing to fallback and limits, 503s dropped to near-zero for Acme but some p95 latency increased. Customer acknowledges.
eng-runtime-jordan: Next steps: collect cores, attach to repro harness with same payload; if OOM reproduces, we'll add guard checks in allocator and a fallback path to avoid segfaults. Create an incident ticket and schedule postmortem.
deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20260318-0914.
sre-maria: saving heap profiles and nvml dumps to /var/preserve/incidents/INC-20260318-0914.
eng-runtime-jordan: Thanks team. Action owners: jordan=debug & repro, ryan=node logs & driver check, maria=artifacts collection, tom=customer comms. We'll reconvene in #incidents in 30m. :calendar:
